metaDescription: We evaluated six miter saws, corded and cordless, 10 and 12 inch, sliding and fixed, on cut capacity, bevel, cut guides and portability to help you pick.
expertTake: The DEWALT DWS780 12 inch double bevel sliding saw is our best overall pick because it combines wide crosscut capacity, dual bevel, a 15 amp motor and a built-in cut line indicator. The SKIL MS6305 10 inch sliding dual bevel is the value pick for homeowners who want a sliding saw without a premium cost. Anyone who only cuts small trim now and then should skip a large sliding saw and consider a compact 7-1/4 inch model.
introParagraphs: A miter saw makes fast, repeatable crosscuts and angled cuts, which is why it sits at the centre of trim carpentry, framing, deck building and picture framing. Set an angle, pull the blade down, and every cut matches the last one.

The choices are blade size, whether the head slides, whether it bevels one way or both, and whether the power comes from a cord or a battery. Capacity, accuracy and the way you set up the saw matter more than any single number on the box.

products.name: DEWALT DWS780 12 Inch Double Bevel Sliding Miter Saw
products.description:
The DEWALT DWS780 is a 12 inch sliding compound miter saw with a 15 amp, 1100 watt, 3,800 RPM motor and a double bevel that tilts both left and right so you do not have to flip the workpiece. The listing highlights the XPS cut line system, an adjustment-free shadow light that shows exactly where the blade will cut, and the sliding head allows wide crosscuts that a fixed saw cannot manage.

The tradeoff is size and weight. A 12 inch sliding saw is large and heavy, and needs a proper stand or bench, so it is more of a shop or garage tool than a quick-carry saw. Compared with the DEWALT DWS715, which is a non-sliding single bevel, the DWS780 gives you much wider capacity and dual bevel, but costs more and takes more space. It suits trim carpenters, deck builders and serious DIY.

Check the fence alignment and detent plate before important cuts, keep the rails clean and lubricated, and use a good blade with the right tooth count for finish or framing. Wear eye and ear protection, and let the blade stop fully before lifting.
products.bestFor: Serious DIYers and trim carpenters who need wide capacity and dual bevel.
pros: Sliding head gives wide crosscut capacity on a 12 inch blade
Double bevel cuts both ways without flipping the workpiece
XPS shadow light shows the cut line without calibration
Fifteen amp motor has the power for hardwoods and thick stock
cons: Large and heavy, so it needs a stand or a dedicated bench
Costs more than fixed-head or 10 inch saws

products.name: SKIL MS6305 10 Inch Dual Bevel Sliding Compound Miter Saw

specList.label: Bevel
specList.value: Dual, with stops at 48, 45 left, 0 and 45 right

products.description:
The SKIL MS6305 is a 10 inch dual bevel sliding compound miter saw with a 15 amp motor turning at 4,800 RPM, four positive bevel stops at 48 and 45 degrees left, 0 and 45 degrees right, and an LED shadow line that the maker says is more precise than a laser. Sliding gives extra crosscut width on a smaller blade, which keeps cost and weight lower than a 12 inch saw.

The tradeoff is capacity and refinement. A 10 inch blade has less depth of cut than a 12 inch blade, so thick posts need two passes, and the build is less robust than DEWALT's professional models. Compared with the DWS780, the SKIL gives similar features at a lower tier but with less maximum capacity and less polish. It suits homeowners doing trim, shelving and decks.

Check fence squareness and bevel stops after unboxing, since cheaper saws sometimes arrive slightly out. Keep the slide rails clean, and replace the stock blade with a finer one for finish work.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want sliding capacity and dual bevel without a premium cost.
pros: Sliding head on a 10 inch blade gives useful extra crosscut width
Dual bevel with four positive stops speeds repeat cuts
LED shadow line shows the cut without a laser
Fifteen amp motor at 4,800 RPM cuts cleanly
cons: Ten inch blade limits depth of cut on thick lumber
Build is less robust than professional sliding saws

products.name: DEWALT DWS715 12 Inch Single Bevel Compound Miter Saw

specList.label: Miter detents
specList.value: Stainless steel plate with 14 positive stops

specList.label: Fence
specList.value: Tall sliding fence supports 5-1/2 inch base vertically

products.description:
The DEWALT DWS715 is a fixed-head 12 inch compound miter saw with a 15 amp motor, a single bevel, a stainless steel detent plate with 14 positive stops and a tall sliding fence that supports 5-1/2 inch baseboard standing up. The large blade gives good cutting depth, and the non-sliding design is simpler and sturdier than a rail system.

The tradeoff is crosscut width. Without a sliding head, the DWS715 has less horizontal capacity than the DWS780, and a single bevel means you flip the workpiece for opposite angles. It is cheaper, lighter and has fewer parts to wear or go out of alignment. It suits framing, fence building and trim work where boards are not very wide.

Check the blade, detent plate and fence alignment, clean sawdust from the pivot and lubricate lightly. Use a quality blade, since a stock blade is a general-purpose compromise.
products.bestFor: Framing and trim where board width is modest and simplicity matters.
pros: Twelve inch blade gives generous cutting depth
Stainless detent plate with 14 positive stops holds angles well
Tall fence supports 5-1/2 inch baseboard standing up
Fixed head has fewer moving parts than a sliding saw
cons: No sliding head limits crosscut width
Single bevel means flipping boards for opposite angles

products.name: Metabo HPT C10FCG2 10 Inch Single Bevel Compound Miter Saw
products.description:
The Metabo HPT C10FCG2 is a second-generation 10 inch single bevel compound miter saw with a 15 amp motor, improved miter scale and controls, a 24 tooth carbide-tipped blade and a weight of only 24 pounds. The light weight is the selling point: it is easy to carry from the truck and set on a bench or stand.

The tradeoff is capability. A fixed 10 inch single bevel saw has limited crosscut and depth, and a 24 tooth blade is a framing blade, not a finish blade, so trim work benefits from a replacement. Compared with the DEWALT DWS715, the Metabo is smaller and lighter, but cuts less depth. It suits jobsite carpentry, deck rails and general DIY.

Check the fence and miter detents, replace the blade for finish work, and keep dust cleared from the base. Use a stand or clamp the saw down.
products.bestFor: Carrying to jobs where weight and simplicity matter most.
pros: Twenty-four pound weight is easy to carry and set up
Fifteen amp motor delivers solid power for a 10 inch saw
Improved miter scale makes angle setting clearer
Carbide-tipped blade is included in the box
cons: Ten inch fixed head limits crosscut width and depth
Stock 24 tooth blade is rough for finish trim work

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR 12 Inch Cordless Double Bevel Sliding Miter Saw
products.description:
The DEWALT DCS785B is a 20V MAX XR cordless 12 inch double bevel sliding miter saw with a stated horizontal capacity of 14 inches and 6-1/2 inch baseboard standing up. Regenerative braking returns energy to the battery, and the tool is sold bare, so you need compatible batteries and a charger. It is the maker's largest-capacity cordless miter saw.

The tradeoff is cost and runtime. A cordless saw costs far more than a corded one once you add batteries, and it runs out of charge on a long job. Compared with the corded DWS780, the cordless gives mobility and no cord, but less sustained power and a larger investment. It suits contractors already on the DEWALT platform and working where outlets are not available.

Charge batteries before a job, keep the rails clean, and check the blade and fence alignment. Store batteries indoors and remove them before blade changes.
products.bestFor: Contractors on the DEWALT platform who need a cord-free sliding saw.
pros: Cord-free operation helps on roofs, decks and sites without power
Fourteen inch horizontal capacity matches corded 12 inch saws
Regenerative braking recovers energy and stops the blade quickly
Dual bevel and a 12 inch blade handle large stock
cons: Much more expensive once batteries and charger are added

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR 10 Inch Cordless Double Bevel Fixed Miter Saw

specList.label: Runtime claim
specList.value: Up to 434 cuts in 3-1/4 in MDF base molding, per the maker

products.description:
The DEWALT DCS714B is a cordless 10 inch double bevel fixed miter saw, sold as a bare tool, that the maker calls its most powerful compact 20V MAX saw. The listing quotes up to 434 cuts in 3-1/4 inch MDF base molding per charge and says it works with the 20V MAX and FLEXVOLT battery range. The bevel gear transmission is meant to improve efficiency.

The tradeoff is that the cut count depends on the battery, and the figure is a maker test of small trim, not a framing job. A fixed head limits crosscut width, and you need to buy batteries separately. Compared with the corded Metabo HPT, the DEWALT is cord-free and double bevel, but more expensive. It suits trim carpenters who move between rooms.

Charge batteries before use, check the fence and blade alignment, and use a trim blade. Store batteries inside and keep the base clear of dust.
products.bestFor: Trim carpenters who want a light, cord-free saw for interior work.
pros: Cordless 10 inch saw is easy to carry between rooms
Double bevel avoids flipping trim pieces
Maker quotes up to 434 cuts on small base molding per charge
Works with the DEWALT 20V MAX battery range
cons: Fixed head limits the width of boards it can cut
Battery and charger are extra, raising the real cost

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 12 inch blade cuts deeper, about 4 to 6 inches of height with a sliding head, and handles thick lumber in one pass. A 10 inch blade is lighter and cheaper but needs two passes on a 4x4. Choose 12 inch for decks and framing and 10 inch for trim and smaller jobs.

A sliding head extends the blade along rails for wide crosscuts, up to about 14 inches on the 12 inch DEWALT saws. A fixed head is simpler and sturdier but limited in width. If you cut shelving or wide boards, buy sliding. For framing and fences, a fixed head is enough.

A single bevel tilts one way, so you flip the workpiece for the opposite angle. A dual bevel tilts both ways, which saves time on crown molding and compound cuts. For occasional trim, single is fine. Daily trim carpenters should buy dual bevel.

Corded saws deliver steady power and cost less. Cordless saws like the DEWALT DCS785B give mobility but need batteries that cost as much as a saw. Choose cordless only if outlets are scarce or you already own the batteries.

LED shadow lines, as on the SKIL and DEWALT DWS780, show where the blade will cut, and are usually better than lasers in bright light. Whatever the guide, check the fence squareness and bevel angle with a square, because factory settings can be slightly out.

Miter saws throw a huge amount of sawdust, and bags capture only a portion, so a vacuum port helps. Weight matters if you carry it: the Metabo HPT weighs 24 pounds, while 12 inch sliding saws weigh far more. A stand or bench makes any saw safer.

specDecoder.meaning: The blade size, usually 7-1/4, 10 or 12 inches. Larger blades cut thicker stock in one pass.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DWS780 and DWS715 use 12 inch blades, while the SKIL and Metabo use 10 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: The widest board the saw can cut at 90 degrees. Sliding saws are far wider than fixed ones.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DCS785B lists up to 14 inches horizontally, which is wide for a cordless saw.

specDecoder.meaning: Single bevel tilts the head in one direction, and dual bevel tilts both. Dual bevel avoids flipping the work.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DWS780, SKIL MS6305 and DCS714B are dual bevel, while the DWS715 and Metabo are single.

specDecoder.meaning: Detent positions that lock the miter at common angles for quick, accurate settings.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DWS715 lists 14 positive stops on a stainless steel plate.

specDecoder.meaning: Amps measure current draw and RPM measures blade speed. Both affect cut quality, but blade type matters just as much.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DWS780 is 15 amp at 3,800 RPM, and the SKIL is 15 amp at 4,800 RPM.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and blade size
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared blade size, crosscut width and bevel capacity from published specifications. The DEWALT DWS780 and DCS785B lead on capacity. Fixed 10 inch saws were rated for lighter work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bevel and miter system
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at single versus dual bevel and the quality of detents. The DWS780 and SKIL dual bevels earned credit for flexibility. Stainless detent plates were rated for accuracy.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cut line and accuracy features
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered LED shadow lines and adjustment features. The XPS system on the DWS780 and the SKIL shadow line help alignment. We noted that every saw needs a square check.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at motor amps, weight and cordless options, using owner feedback patterns. The Metabo HPT at 24 pounds is easiest to carry. Cordless models were assessed for cost and runtime.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each saw to a realistic user, from trim carpenter to deck builder. A bigger saw is not always better value. We judged by fit rather than raw capacity.

cards.label: Sliding
cards.text: A saw like the DWS780 or SKIL cuts wide boards and shelving, but is larger and has rails to maintain.

cards.label: Fixed
cards.text: A saw like the DWS715 or Metabo is simpler, lighter and sturdier, but limited in crosscut width.

howToChoose.note: Choose sliding if you cut wide boards and fixed if you mostly cut framing and trim.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Dual bevel, a tall fence for base, positive stops and a fine-tooth blade. A good cut line guide saves rework.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DWS780 and SKIL give dual bevel, and the DCS714B is a light cordless option.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut daily or need large capacity. The DWS780 and DCS785B justify it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You build the occasional shelf or fence. The Metabo or SKIL is plenty.

maintenance.task: Check fence and bevel with a square
maintenance.why: Factory settings can be slightly out and drift with use. A square check prevents ruined stock.
Sawdust packs the rails and causes sticking. A dry lubricant keeps the slide smooth.
A dull blade burns wood and strains the motor. A sharp finish blade gives cleaner trim cuts.

maintenance.task: Clear dust from the base and port
maintenance.why: Packed dust interferes with the miter scale and the detents. A brush or vacuum keeps them clear.
Worn brushes weaken the motor, and a damaged cord is a hazard. Replace worn parts.

faq.q: Is a sliding miter saw worth it?
faq.a: If you cut wide boards or shelving, yes, because it extends crosscut capacity. For framing and trim, a fixed saw is simpler, lighter and less expensive.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a miter saw?
faq.a: A fixed 10 inch saw costs the least, while a 12 inch sliding dual bevel costs more and a cordless one costs the most. Spend for capacity you will actually use.

faq.q: How long does a miter saw last?
faq.a: A decent saw lasts many years with care. Brushes, blades and the slide rails are the wear items, and keeping dust out extends life.

faq.q: Does a bigger blade mean a better saw?
faq.a: Not always. A 12 inch blade cuts deeper but is heavier, while a 10 inch blade is easier to carry and often enough for trim.

faq.q: Is a miter saw safe for beginners?
faq.a: It is safe when used correctly, but the blade is exposed and kickback can occur. Clamp the work, keep hands clear, wear eye and ear protection, and let the blade stop before lifting.
A stand or bench makes cuts safer and more accurate, especially with a heavy sliding saw. Long boards need support on both sides.
